golden_test_names: TIME - INTERVAL with INT64_MIN microseconds should throw an error, not overflow
TIMETZ - INTERVAL with INT64_MIN microseconds should throw an error, not overflow
reproduction: build/release/duckdb -c "SELECT TIME '12:00:00' - INTERVAL '-4611686018427387904 microseconds -4611686018427387904 microseconds';"  (and the same with TIMETZ '12:00:00+00'). The interval literal sums to INT64_MIN microseconds.
observed_failure_at_parent: No error is raised: the query returns a silently wrong time value (07:59:05.224192 / 07:59:05.224192+00 for 12:00:00) because negating INT64_MIN microseconds overflows. Buggy code confirmed present at parent: SubtractTimeOperator::Operation does `right.micros = -right.micros;` with no bounds check (inspection of src/function/scalar/operator/subtract.cpp).
verified: Both directions observed on bench-base:ubuntu-24.04 (gcc 13): at parent_commit the CLI returns the wrong TIME/TIMETZ value with no error; at fix_commit the same query raises 'Out of Range Error: Interval micros value out of range'. Parent lacked the bounds checks by inspection.
install_recipe: apt-get update && apt-get install -y g++ gcc make cmake ninja-build python3 git; cd duckdb; cmake -G Ninja -B build/release -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DBUILD_UNITTESTS=1 -DEXTENSION_STATIC_BUILD=1 -DBUILD_EXTENSIONS=core_functions; ninja -C build/release; CLI binary is build/release/duckdb
issue_paraphrase: Subtracting an interval whose microseconds component is the minimum 64-bit signed integer from a TIME or TIMETZ value does not fail. Because the internal negation of that extreme value overflows, the query returns a completely wrong time (e.g. 07:59:05 for 12:00:00) instead of raising an out-of-range error, for both TIME and TIMETZ operands. The result is silently incorrect with no diagnostic, so users get garbage data from valid-looking arithmetic.
fix_summary: Added explicit checks in SubtractTimeOperator::Operation (TIME and TIMETZ overloads) and in Interval::Invert that throw OutOfRangeException when the interval's days/micros/months field equals its numeric minimum, before any negation happens.
notes: Self-contained CLI reproduction, no network, no fixtures. .test oracle file was added by the fix commit itself. Reproduce via the CLI only; BUILD_UNITTESTS is only needed if the author wants to run the .test file through build/release/test/unittest.

golden_test_names: missing named parameters must be reported in declaration order, not hash order
reproduction: build/release/duckdb with input: PREPARE q03 AS SELECT $aa, $bb, $cc, $dd, $ee; EXECUTE q03(aa := 1, bb := 2);
observed_failure_at_parent: The missing-parameter error lists the names in hash order instead of declaration order: 'Invalid Input Error: Values were not provided for the following parameters: ee, cc, dd' (declared order is $aa,$bb,$cc,$dd,$ee). Buggy code confirmed present at parent: MissingValuesException collects into identifier_set_t (std::unordered_set) whose iteration order is hash-bucket order (inspection of src/include/duckdb/main/prepared_statement.hpp).
verified: Both directions observed: at parent_commit the message reads 'ee, cc, dd'; at fix_commit the same input reads 'cc, dd, ee'. The ordering was stable across repeated runs on the same build.
install_recipe: apt-get update && apt-get install -y g++ gcc make cmake ninja-build python3 git; cd duckdb; cmake -G Ninja -B build/release -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DBUILD_UNITTESTS=1 -DEXTENSION_STATIC_BUILD=1 -DBUILD_EXTENSIONS=core_functions; ninja -C build/release; CLI binary is build/release/duckdb
issue_paraphrase: When executing a prepared statement that uses named parameters and only some of them are supplied, the error message that lists which parameters are missing presents them in an unpredictable order instead of the order in which they appear in the statement. A statement declaring five parameters and supplying two may report the three missing ones as 'ee, cc, dd', which is confusing and unstable, and the message format differs from what users and tools expect.
fix_summary: MissingValuesException now collects (index, name) pairs using the parameter index already assigned by the parser and sorts by index before formatting, so missing named parameters are always reported in declaration order.
notes: Self-contained CLI reproduction via PREPARE/EXECUTE, no network. The oracle must assert the exact error text (order matters). The fix touches only a header so any patch set must edit the header; rebuilds of that header propagate to much of the tree.

golden_test_names: %c writes a single raw byte - it may not produce invalid UTF8
observed_failure_at_parent: Plain printf('%c', 255) fails with 'Invalid Input Error: invalid lead byte detected in Utf8Proc::UTF8ToCodepoint, likely due to invalid UTF-8'; lower(printf('%c', 255)) throws 'INTERNAL Error: Scalar function "lower" threw an execution error, but the function is not marked as fallible - the function must call SetFallible()...' plus a stack trace (trim behaves similarly). Buggy code confirmed present at parent: PrintfFunction writes the format result raw with no UTF-8 validation (no Utf8Proc::IsValid call).
verified: Both directions observed: at parent_commit the queries raise the internal UTF-8/INTERNAL errors above; at fix_commit both queries raise a clean 'Invalid Input Error: Invalid UTF8 produced by format string "%c" - note that %c writes a single byte, use chr(...) to write a Unicode code point'.
install_recipe: apt-get update && apt-get install -y g++ gcc make cmake ninja-build python3 git; cd duckdb; cmake -G Ninja -B build/release -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DBUILD_UNITTESTS=1 -DEXTENSION_STATIC_BUILD=1 -DBUILD_EXTENSIONS=core_functions; ninja -C build/release; CLI binary is build/release/duckdb
issue_paraphrase: The printf/format %c conversion writes its argument's low byte verbatim, so formatting a codepoint above 127 produces a string containing invalid UTF-8 bytes. Any subsequent use of that string, even just displaying the result, then fails with low-level UTF-8 decoding errors, and string functions applied to the result crash out with an INTERNAL error and a stack trace instead of a clear user-facing message.
fix_summary: PrintfFunction now validates the formatted result with Utf8Proc::IsValid and throws a helpful InvalidInputException (shared by printf and format) when the result is not valid UTF-8, pointing users to chr() for writing code points.
notes: Self-contained CLI reproduction, no network. printf/format live in the core_functions extension, which must be statically built (EXTENSION_STATIC_BUILD=1, BUILD_EXTENSIONS=core_functions) for the functions to exist in the CLI binary.

golden_test_names: parallel CSV reader handles \r\r\n line endings without duplicate rows
reproduction: Extract data/csv/test/rrrn_parallel_test.csv (a 10K-row CSV using \r\r\n line endings) from the fix commit; then run: PRAGMA verify_parallelism; SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM read_csv('rrrn_parallel_test.csv', auto_detect=false, header=true, delim=',', columns={'id':'BIGINT','val':'VARCHAR'}, strict_mode=false, ignore_errors=true, max_line_size=2048, buffer_size=4096, parallel=true)), (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM read_csv('rrrn_parallel_test.csv', auto_detect=false, header=true, delim=',', columns={'id':'BIGINT','val':'VARCHAR'}, strict_mode=false, ignore_errors=true, max_line_size=2048, buffer_size=4096, parallel=false));
observed_failure_at_parent: Parallel read returns 10002 rows while sequential read of the same file returns 10000 (duplicate rows, stable across 3 runs); a GROUP BY id HAVING count(*)>1 check reports duplicates. Buggy code confirmed present at parent: ProcessOverBufferValue has no pre_carry_pos / early-return guard (the fix symbol is absent).
verified: Both directions observed on the same host file: parent_commit parallel=10002 / sequential=10000 (3/3 runs); fix_commit parallel=10000 / sequential=10000 and zero duplicate ids. Uses PRAGMA verify_parallelism (registered unconditionally in release builds).
install_recipe: apt-get update && apt-get install -y g++ gcc make cmake ninja-build python3 git; cd duckdb; cmake -G Ninja -B build/release -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DBUILD_UNITTESTS=1 -DEXTENSION_STATIC_BUILD=1 -DBUILD_EXTENSIONS=core_functions; ninja -C build/release; CLI binary is build/release/duckdb
issue_paraphrase:
Reading a CSV file whose lines end with the '
' sequence (common output of certain Windows tools) using the parallel CSV reader can silently return more rows than the file actually contains: rows near buffer boundaries get counted twice, so a 10,000-row file yields 10,002 rows while the sequential reader returns exactly 10,000. Parallel and sequential scans of the same file must agree on the row count.
fix_summary: In StringValueScanner::ProcessOverBufferValue, when the newline-consuming carry loop consumed characters without adding a row and the previous buffer already fully counted that row, the scanner now returns early instead of falling through to double-count the next row. The guard fires only when the first consumed character is '\r' so '\r\n' endings are unaffected.
notes: Self-contained, no network. The regression .test file at the fix commit uses the in-tree fixture data/csv/test/rrrn_parallel_test.csv; at HEAD it was reworked by follow-ups 1f8535d21f, 8d7ba01549 and 41cf95510ff9 (comment/test-only commits, 41cf95510ff9 changes no logic) to generate boundary-exact files, so the author should copy the fixture or the generated-file SQL from the HEAD .test. Reproduction verified with the 10K-row fixture and buffer_size=4096; keep PRAGMA verify_parallelism in the oracle. The visibility of the bug depends on buffer geometry, so prefer the exact fixture.

golden_test_names: NULL is not a valid value for sequence options (START NULL / START WITH NULL / MINVALUE NULL / MAXVALUE NULL / INCREMENT BY NULL)
reproduction: build/release/duckdb -c "CREATE SEQUENCE wrongseq START WITH NULL;" (also valid: MINVALUE NULL, MAXVALUE NULL, INCREMENT BY NULL)
observed_failure_at_parent: CREATE SEQUENCE with a NULL option crashes with 'INTERNAL Error: Calling GetValue on a value that is NULL' followed by 'This error signals an assertion failure within DuckDB...' and a stack trace, instead of a clean parser error. Buggy code confirmed present at parent: the transformer reads option values with Value::GetValue and has no NULL guards.
verified: Both directions observed: parent_commit raises the INTERNAL/assertion error for every NULL option; fix_commit raises clean 'Parser Error: START value must not be NULL' / 'MINVALUE must not be NULL' / 'MAXVALUE must not be NULL' / 'INCREMENT must not be NULL'.
install_recipe: apt-get update && apt-get install -y g++ gcc make cmake ninja-build python3 git; cd duckdb; cmake -G Ninja -B build/release -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DBUILD_UNITTESTS=1 -DEXTENSION_STATIC_BUILD=1 -DBUILD_EXTENSIONS=core_functions; ninja -C build/release; CLI binary is build/release/duckdb
issue_paraphrase: Creating a sequence with a NULL value for any of its options (START with, MINVALUE, MAXVALUE, or INCREMENT BY) crashes the server with an internal assertion failure instead of reporting a normal parser error. Users passing NULL where a number is required, e.g. via a parameterized script, get an unhandled internal error and a stack trace rather than a clear message that the option must not be NULL.
fix_summary: The CREATE SEQUENCE parser transformation now explicitly rejects NULL for INCREMENT, MINVALUE, MAXVALUE and START with descriptive ParserExceptions instead of hitting generic NULL value handling.
notes: Self-contained CLI reproduction, no network, no fixtures. Oracle can assert the <REGEX> parser error lines as in the .test file.

golden_test_names: errors thrown by the reduce lambda propagate as clean errors, not INTERNAL errors
reproduction: build/release/duckdb -c "SELECT list_reduce([1, 2], lambda x, y: error('test error'));" (also: SELECT list_reduce(['1', 'a'], lambda x, y: (x::INT + y::INT)::VARCHAR);)
observed_failure_at_parent: The lambda's error surfaces as 'INTERNAL Error: Scalar function "list_reduce" threw an execution error, but the function is not marked as fallible - the function must call SetFallible(). Error: test error' plus a stack trace, instead of the clean error the lambda raised. Buggy code confirmed present at parent: ListReduceFun never calls SetFallible().
verified: Both directions observed: parent_commit raises the INTERNAL error with stack trace for both the error() lambda and the failing-cast lambda; fix_commit raises a clean 'Invalid Input Error: test error' for the first and 'Conversion Error: Could not convert string 'a' to INT32...' for the second.
install_recipe: apt-get update && apt-get install -y g++ gcc make cmake ninja-build python3 git; cd duckdb; cmake -G Ninja -B build/release -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DBUILD_UNITTESTS=1 -DEXTENSION_STATIC_BUILD=1 -DBUILD_EXTENSIONS=core_functions; ninja -C build/release; CLI binary is build/release/duckdb
issue_paraphrase: When the reduction lambda passed to list_reduce throws an error at runtime — for example by calling the error() function or by doing a cast that fails inside the lambda — the user sees an INTERNAL error with a stack trace saying the function is 'not marked as fallible' instead of the actual error message. Errors raised inside lambda bodies should propagate to the user as ordinary Invalid Input or Conversion errors, the same way they do for other list functions.
fix_summary: Marks ListReduceFun as fallible (fun.SetFallible()) so exceptions raised by the user's lambda propagate as clean user-facing errors instead of INTERNAL errors.
notes: Self-contained CLI reproduction, no network. list_reduce lives in the core_functions extension; the build must statically link it (EXTENSION_STATIC_BUILD=1, BUILD_EXTENSIONS=core_functions).
